info.title: DevResponse Administrator API
info.description: Administrator console API (`/api/administrator`). Authenticate EITHER with the Better Auth **session cookie** (send credentials with the request; every **mutation** then also requires an `Origin` or `Referer` header matching a trusted origin — the CSRF guard — which a browser sets itself and a server-side caller must add) OR with a **bearer** API key / JWT, whose effective authority is the intersection of its scopes and the permissions of its owner and which is exempt from the origin guard. The one exception is `DELETE /users/{id}/impersonate`, which bypasses the permission guard by design and is therefore **cookie-session only** (see that operation). Org admins are scoped to their own organization (out-of-scope resources return 404, not 403). Errors use `{ error, message, requestId }`; every response carries an `x-request-id` header.

cookieSession.name: __Secure-better-auth.session_token
cookieSession.description: Better Auth session cookie. The name carries Better Auth's `__Secure-` prefix on any https origin (production); only a plain-http dev origin uses the bare `better-auth.session_token`. The value is the SIGNED cookie value exactly as a real browser session holds it — not a session id or token from the `session` table, which Better Auth will reject. Browser clients send it automatically (`credentials: "include"`); a server-side caller forwards the `Cookie` header and, on every mutation, adds a trusted `Origin` header (the CSRF guard).

bearerAuth.description: A DevResponse API key (`drk_…`) or a JWT minted at `POST /api/v1/auth/token`, in `Authorization: Bearer …`. Accepted on every administrator operation that lists it (all of them except `DELETE /users/{id}/impersonate`, which is cookie-only; both credential paths are disabled by default: `API_KEYS_ENABLED` / `API_JWT_ENABLED`). The credential's effective authority is `scopes ∩ owner permissions`: an operation needs the owner to hold the permission AND the credential to carry a scope covering it (e.g. `admin.users.read`, or a prefix scope such as `admin.users.*`), else `403 forbidden`. Bearer callers are exempt from the `Origin` guard (a bearer cannot be attached by a cross-site page).

Unauthorized.description: No session cookie and no bearer credential resolved (`unauthenticated`) — also the answer for a revoked/expired bearer or a disabled credential path.

Forbidden.description: `forbidden`: the caller lacks the permission (or, for a bearer, a covering scope), their account/membership is not active, or the action is out of their org scope. `untrusted_origin`: a cookie-session MUTATION arrived without an `Origin`/`Referer` header matching a trusted origin (CSRF guard; never returned to bearer callers).

NotFound.description: Not found (or out of org scope)

Unprocessable.description: Unprocessable — `invalid_scope` with the scopes the caller may not grant

RateLimited.description: Too many requests (`rate_limited`); retry after `retryAfter` seconds

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait — the same value as the body's `retryAfter`.

AdminError.description: Administrator error envelope. `adminErrorResponse` may spread extra non-secret fields for specific codes — see `RateLimitedError` / `UnprocessableError`.

retryAfter.description: Seconds until the bucket refills enough to retry.

ungrantableScopes.description: Requested scopes outside the caller's own authority (permissions ∩ credential scopes).

SessionItem.description: One active Better Auth session, projected to non-secret metadata. The session token is never exposed; revoke by `id`.

impersonatedBy.description: Better Auth user id of the impersonating admin, when this is an impersonation session.

ids.description: 1–500 app user ids, or the string `*` (the only accepted string) to select by `filters`.

filters.description: Selection filters for `ids: "*"` (ignored for an explicit id list).

status.description: A list of statuses, or one status as a bare string.

roleId.description: Optional app role granted on acceptance; must belong to this org.

AuthPolicySettings.description: The raw policy override row; null when the organization inherits the platform default.

allowedAuthMethods.description: null = every enabled auth method is accepted.

autoApproveEmailDomains.description: Lowercased domains; null = no domain auto-approval.

AuthPolicyEffective.description: The resolved policy that actually governs sign-ups for this scope.

UpdateAuthPolicyRequest.description: A COMPLETE policy — there is no partial update; PATCH creates or replaces the row.

OutboxDetail.description: One outbox row with its rendered bodies. Bodies are the REDACTED rendering stored at insert time: one-time reset / verification / invitation tokens read `[redacted]`.

clientRowId.description: OAuth-client row id — the `{id}` of the agent operations.

status.description: Derived lifecycle status (pending ⇒ awaiting approval; revoked ⇒ client inactive).

pendingCount.description: Agents awaiting approval across the caller's WHOLE scope — independent of the page and filter.

activated.description: false when the agent was already active (idempotent).

alreadyRevoked.description: Present (true) when the client was not active any more — a no-op.

delete.description: Cookie session only. Unlike every other administrator operation this one does not go through the permission guard — the authority to stop derives from the live session BEING an impersonation session — so it always enforces the `Origin`/`Referer` (CSRF) check and always requires a session cookie. A bearer credential cannot authenticate here: it answers `403 untrusted_origin` (no `Origin`) or `401 unauthenticated`. `400 not_impersonating` when the session is real but not an impersonation.

delete.description: `sessionId` is the `id` of a `SessionItem` from the list — never the session token. The server resolves the id to the token itself (review #67/#194); an id that is not one of the target user's active sessions is `404 session_not_found`.

get.description: Streams the resource as CSV (capped at `X-Export-Limit` rows). Filters are the SAME `filter[...]` parameters the resource's list endpoint accepts — the route allow-lists them per resource (`ALLOWED_FILTERS_BY_RESOURCE`) and silently drops any other: `users` → status; `audit` → event_type, outcome, actor, app_user_id, organization_id, target_application_id, created_at[from|to]; `organizations` → status, is_default; `roles` → organization, scope; `permissions` → none; `memberships` → status, organization_id, source_provider; `enterprise-apps` → status, organization_id. Rate-limited per actor (3 burst / one per 20 s).

get.summary: List self-registered MCP agents (pending first) with the scope-wide pending count
get.description: Requires `admin.clients.read`. Pending agents always sort first, then `sort` (`created_at` | `name`, default `created_at.desc`). `q` is not supported here. `pendingCount` counts every pending agent in the caller's scope regardless of page/filter, so a badge stays truthful on any view.

parameters.name: filter[status]
parameters.description: Derived lifecycle status; an unrecognised value applies no filter.

patch.description: Requires `admin.clients.manage`. Scopes are validated against the caller's own authority (permissions, and for a bearer caller its own scopes) — over-granting is `422 invalid_scope` listing `ungrantableScopes`. A granted scope only takes effect where the service account also holds the matching permission.

delete.description: Requires `admin.clients.manage`. The service account is left intact for the audit trail; an already-revoked client answers `{ ok: true, alreadyRevoked: true }`.

post.summary: Approve a pending agent (activate its service account)
post.description: Requires `admin.clients.manage`. Idempotent — an already-active agent answers `{ ok: true, activated: false }`.
